topology.caption: Complete native TER list construction and the isolated prepared reporting boundary used in Sections 7–8.6. The production binary-root branch is untimed in those prepared-reporter experiments; Section 8.7 evaluates the staged solver integration separately. Captured native L1 lists provide arithmetic keys, stored residues, coordinate data and EntryIds. The prepared reporter outputs alone do not certify a solver solution.
topology.description: Flow diagram: 18 logical L3 lists merge to 9 L2 lists and then 3 L1 lists. A dashed, untimed production L0 branch is separate. A downward capture branch supplies an isolated prepared arithmetic reporter, which produces a residue-exact identity multiset and separate finite-predicate count.

pipeline.caption: ARWLF's routing, necessary byte predicates and exact survivor resolution. The arithmetic reporter retains every full quotient equality and original posting multiplicity. Residue-exact identities are collected before the attached finite test-parent predicate of Section 2.3, which differs from the production binary-root rule.
pipeline.description: Five sequential boxes show family carry calculation, 13-bit leaf routing, one-row-by-16-lane byte tests, exact full-key resolution, and stored-residue checking. Output branches separately to the residue-exact multiset and the finite-predicate counter; n=108 finite counts are negative 2, zero 86, positive 20.

dense.caption: All 29 declared authentic dimension-108 cell speedups, grouped by captured root and calibration role. Diamonds use the final protocol (seven timed rounds) and circles discovery (three); dashed segments show each root's geometric mean. Aggregate labels are case-pooled geometric means. Repeated cells share their root and are not independent instances.
dense.description: Scatterplot of all 29 K2/ARWLF median ratios across six root-seed groups. Calibration points are teal; holdout points orange. Diamonds indicate seven-round final anchors and circles three-round discovery cases. Per-root geometric means are dashed. Most ratios lie near 47 to 54; the 0x2003 final anchor is about 78, with holdout discovery points near 62 to 63 and one near 47.

crossover.caption: Controlled source-thinning crossover for three calibration dimension-108 roots. Discovery lines use geometric means over three thinning seeds; plotted L is their geometric-mean observed census occupancy. Open diamonds are separate final-protocol confirmations using seed 0xA11CE001. Ratios below one favor ARWLF. Lines connect measured points, not a fitted or universal threshold. Target L=96 is unreachable for root 0x1001.
crossover.description: Log-log plot of ARWLF/rival time ratio against observed packet occupancy L for three source-thinned roots. Discovery averages over three thinning seeds are colored connected circles; final confirmations are open diamonds. Ratios exceed one at L=1 and fall below one near L=2, approaching about 0.03 at the densest tested controls.

target.caption: Absolute median times under target-only thinning with fixed source-pair mass on three calibration roots. Filled points use discovery (one warmup, three timed rounds); open full-density references use final anchors (three warmups, seven timed rounds). Dashed connections mark the protocol change. Target thinning is a controlled sensitivity experiment, not a smaller-dimension authentic benchmark.
target.description: Three side-by-side panels show absolute median times for K2, K2-WIDE and ARWLF as target retention increases from one-eighth to one. K2 and K2-WIDE become much slower with denser targets, while ARWLF changes more modestly. Open full-density points use seven-round final anchors; filled thinned points use three-round discovery cases, with dashed segments separating the protocols.
